edges.description: p53 degradation abolishes G1/S and G2/M checkpoints
E2F release activates genes required for DNA replication
Infection of the oropharyngeal epithelium is what introduces the E6 oncoprotein, so the exposure initiates the earliest curated mechanism.

nodes.description: HPV E6 oncoprotein recruits the E3 ubiquitin ligase E6AP to target p53 for proteasomal degradation, eliminating DNA damage checkpoints and allowing survival of cells with genomic instability. Unlike HPV-negative HNSCC, TP53 mutations are rare in HPV-positive tumors.

HPV E7 oncoprotein binds and degrades the retinoblastoma protein (pRB), releasing E2F transcription factors to drive S-phase entry. This causes compensatory overexpression of p16INK4a, which serves as a clinical biomarker for HPV-associated tumors.

biological_processes: G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle

nodes.description: Oral high-risk HPV infection is the etiologic driver of this entity, which is what separates it from HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The initiating event is viral rather than a host genetic lesion.

evidence.reference_title: Deciphering the interplay of HPV infection, MHC-II expression, and CXCL13+ CD4+ T cell activation in oropharyngeal cancer: implications for immunotherapy
evidence.snippet: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection has become an important etiological driver of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), leading to unique tumor characteristics.
